title: PHASE A SPACE BASED RE-ENTRY MONITOR - EXPRO+
description: Objectives and TasksThe activity aims to reach a preliminary design for a dedicated mission that will measure from orbit the destructive re-entry of artificial space objects in the Earth's atmosphere by means of a dedicated set of sensors. Pre-cursor sensor level activities haveidentified AlO (aluminium oxide band and associate lithium markers) and SWIR (shortwave infrared) as the most promising and accessible wavelengths from orbit that most re-entry events of artificial will have in common. The study shall establish the system level accommodation of such a sensor suite on a large CubeSat or small satellite platform with capable AOCS suite for pointing and orbit control.As uncontrolled or controlled re-entry events can occur anywhere on the globe, it is envisaged the satelliteplatform shall be in a relatively high orbit to ensure the field of view of the sensors can point to the re-entry streaks generated(which can last for 100'sof km) and preferential observation geometries (such as re-entry event in the Earth shadow) can be reached on average for 1 out of the on average 3 re-entries daily within the forecasting period of a ground segment (roughly two days prior to the event). The mobility needs of the platform shall thus be an integral part of the phase A level tradeoffs.To prepare for the above-described mission, the proposed activity will assess the overall feasibility of the mission and specifically include: Mission and requirements definition: redefine in detail the purpose and mission objectives deriving consistently the satellite system, theorbital, and the groundsegment requirements. These shall be derived from the identified need on regularly observing re-entry events. Conceptual design: based on the mission definition and system requirements, a conceptual design of the satellite will be developed. This includes the basiclayout of the satellite, the platform mass and size, the orbit, the major components and subsystems considering as well launch vehicle, and groundsegment. Definition of the payload (e.g. hyperspectral cameras and SWIR imagers). Identify all critical items (< TRL 6) and derive technology development plans for each including definition of the VV approach. Preliminary cost and schedule: estimate of costs and schedules is developed based on the conceptual design, and the system requirementsto be below 25MEUR. Risk assessment: risks associated with the mission and satellite design will be identified, evaluated, andassessed. Feasibility analysis: the feasibility of the mission and satellite design is assessed, taking into account technical, cost, and schedule considerations. Analysis of the commercialisation opportunities related to the mission concept and the related technologies.

title: EARTH ACTION - GDA NEXT GENERATION MAINSTREAMING ELEMENT ON POVERTY-FRAGILITY-DISASTER NEXUS - EXPRO+
description: The activity aims to support the mainstreaming and operational adoption of EO-based solutions for fragility, poverty and disaster-related applications, building on the priorities and operational needs identified through the co-design process with IFIs.Focus willbe given to priority areas such as measuring fragility, damage assessment and service disruption in conflict-affected settings, andother applications supporting decision-making in fragile and crisis contexts.The activity will address the conditions required forsustained uptake, including validation, usability, interoperability with existing user systems and analytical frameworks, scalability,and integration into institutional workflows. It will also assess suitable delivery, governance and business models to enable the continued operational use of the developed indicators, data products and analytical capabilities beyond individual demonstrations.Theoverall objective is to develop and operationalise sustainable EO-enabled capabilities that can be embedded in the operational processes of IFIs.

title: QUANTUM RESISTANT SYMMETRIC-BASED CRYPTOGRAPHIC DEVICE FOR TC/TM PROTECTION - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To implement, validate and test a cryptographic device for security protection of TC/TM.Description:Security protection of TC/TM utilizing cryptographic device capability shall be compliant with correspondingCCSDS standards, implementing SDLS (SpaceData Link Security protocol) and SDLS EP (ExtendedProcedures). It will also include the development of the corresponding Ground Segment Key Management module (unless the needed ground segment capability is already available through COTS or other developments). The implementation will be on hardware; software implementations (not part of this activity) can complement the development for smallsatellites with low assurance requirements or cubesats. The device will target the protection of TC and TM communication links.Theactivity will develop an engineering model, using a hardware based optimised implementations ofauthenticated encryption. Specifically, it will develop:- Engineering Model (EM): flight representative hardware in form, fit and function (including timing and interfaces), allowing functional qualification.- Unit tester / testbench (hardware) that allows to send data to the EM through any of its interfaces up to themaximum data rates supported by the EM (this includes encryption/decryption of data sent/received to the EM).Unit tester / testbench will also record data sent and received to the module.- Ground key management module (software) being ableto manage the cryptographic parameters and keys of the unit tester and EM.

title: GT17-670GD - EVOLVED OPERATIONAL USER INTERFACES (EXPRO+)
description: Existing operational user interfaces for ground segment are primarily built on aging software platforms characterized by deprecated technologies, a monolithic architecture and rigid implementation. While these legacy platforms provide stability for established scenarios, it struggles to adapt to modern operational demands specifically the introduction of remote operations, cloud infrastructure management, and the seamless integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Building on the EGS-CC WebUI and the PulseUI, a specialized WebUI branch tailored for operational environments, the new approach has enabled support for comprehensive UI testing, facilitate remote control capabilities, and better align with the microservices architecture backends. To overcome these challenges and achieve the goals of the project, an architectural and design approach based on the following will be required: - Web-Based Architecture: To guarantee high flexibility and stability. - Unified Design System: Establishing a common look and feel across the ground segment.  - Industry-Standard Framework Principles: Adopting the principles of established UI frameworks (such as Material Design). This will provide a comprehensive suite of reusable components, complete with intuitive documentation and tutorials, hence mitigates the risk of "technology islands".
